name: Section 1 Quiz 1: Databricks Machine Learning
description:
Section 1 quiz: Databricks Machine Learning

Pick one answer per question unless stated otherwise.

items.prompt: A team currently runs training jobs on a standard Databricks Runtime and spends time installing and version-matching ML libraries. What is the main advantage of switching to Databricks Runtime for Machine Learning?

choices.text: It automatically tunes hyperparameters for any model trained on the cluster
It includes popular ML libraries and MLflow preinstalled and tested together
It removes the need to track experiments, because every run is logged to Unity Catalog automatically
It guarantees higher model accuracy than a standard runtime

items.prompt: A data scientist runs Databricks AutoML on a tabular dataset to predict customer churn. Which is a benefit of this approach?

choices.text: The best model is deployed to production automatically, with no review step
AutoML eliminates the need for any data exploration or feature engineering
AutoML supports only deep learning models
Each trial generates a notebook with source code that can be inspected and modified, giving a quick, transparent baseline

items.prompt: An organization has three workspaces attached to one Unity Catalog metastore. Teams want to share and discover features, with centralized access control and lineage. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: Feature tables in Unity Catalog, governed by UC privileges, discoverable from any workspace on the metastore, with lineage tracked
Workspace-level feature tables, with notebook ACLs controlling access
Workspace-level feature tables, replicated by Databricks to every workspace in the account
Unity Catalog feature tables, which require Delta Sharing to be read from a second workspace on the same metastore

items.prompt: A data scientist has a Delta table in Unity Catalog with customer features. What must be true for it to be used as a feature table?

choices.text: It must be registered with FeatureStoreClient.register_table
It must have a primary key constraint
It must live in a catalog named feature_store
It must be an external table with Change Data Feed enabled

items.prompt: A data scientist builds a training set with FeatureLookup objects and create_training_set, then logs the model with FeatureEngineeringClient.log_model and that training set. What does this enable when scoring later?

choices.text: The feature values are stored inside the model as constants, so the feature tables are no longer needed
The model must be retrained every time a feature table is updated
score_batch needs only the lookup keys, and features are retrieved from the feature tables using metadata packaged with the model
The model can be scored only through a real-time endpoint

items.prompt: A real-time endpoint must fetch customer features within milliseconds. The same features are also used for nightly training. Which design is best?

choices.text: Query the offline Delta feature table directly on every request
Recompute features from raw data inside every request
Use an online store only, and train from it
Keep the offline feature table for training and batch scoring, and publish it to an online store for low-latency lookups

items.prompt: Several runs in one experiment logged rmse (lower is better). Which MLflow Client API call returns the best run?

choices.text: mlflow.get_best_run(experiment_id, metric="rmse")
client.search_runs([exp_id], order_by=["metrics.rmse DESC"], max_results=1)
client.get_run(exp_id).data.metrics["rmse"]
client.search_runs([exp_id], order_by=["metrics.rmse ASC"], max_results=1)

items.prompt: Inside an active MLflow run, you want to record validation RMSE at each epoch and attach a saved confusion.png file. Which pair of calls is correct?

choices.text: mlflow.log_metric("rmse", value, step=epoch) and mlflow.log_artifact("confusion.png")
mlflow.log_param("rmse", value) and mlflow.log_artifact("confusion.png")
mlflow.log_metric("confusion.png", path) and mlflow.log_param("rmse", value)
mlflow.set_tag("rmse", value) and mlflow.log_metric("confusion.png", path)

items.prompt: While logging a scikit-learn model, you want to register it in Unity Catalog. Which registered_model_name is valid?

choices.text: "iris_model"
"ml_team.iris_model"
"prod.ml_team.iris_model"
"/Shared/models/iris_model"

items.prompt: Inference jobs load models:/prod.ml.fraud@Champion. Version 7 passed validation and should replace the current champion without changing any inference code. Which call does this?

choices.text: client.transition_model_version_stage("prod.ml.fraud", 7, stage="Production")
client.set_registered_model_alias("prod.ml.fraud", "Champion", 7)
client.set_model_version_tag("prod.ml.fraud", 7, "Champion", "true")
Register a new model named fraud_champion and update the inference code to load it
